sentences.text: Abyssosaurus possessed a skull that was unusually short and triangular compared to other plesiosaurs, featuring very large eye sockets. Parts of its skeleton retain juvenile traits known as paedomorphosis, a condition seen in various deep-sea vertebrates.

The gastralia and flippers were very robust due to pachyostosis, a condition where bones are thickened with dense tissue that would have reduced buoyancy. The gastralia were unusually thickened, particularly in the center.
This animal had an estimated body length of 6.7 to 7 meters and a body mass of 1.24 metric tons.
Aside from Muraenosaurus, Abyssosaurus is the only cryptoclidid known to preserve a prootic bone, which is more massive in Abyssosaurus.
The neck column is incomplete, preserving only forty-four vertebrae. There were twenty dorsal vertebrae, or twenty-three if pectoral vertebrae are included.
The clavicles were greatly atrophied.
Fossil remains tentatively identified as a fetus were found alongside the holotype, suggesting the species reproduced by giving birth to live young.
The retention of juvenile traits in an adult skeleton indicates a unique developmental pattern for this marine reptile.
Vasily V. Mita discovered a partial plesiosaur skeleton in Chuvashia, Russia, in 1992.
Additional remains were discovered in 1998, expanding the initial collection of twenty cervical vertebrae.
The holotype specimen was discovered in Chuvashia and dates to the late Hauterivian, approximately 133 to 130 million years ago.
In 2011, Alexander Yu Berezin designated the specimen as the holotype for the new species Abyssosaurus nataliae.
The genus Abyssosaurus was described by Alexander Yu Berezin in 2011, and the genus was formally named by Alexander Yu. Berezin in 2011, with the type species designated as Abyssosaurus nataliae.
The type species, A. nataliae, was named by Alexander Yu Berezin in 2011 after his wife, Nataliya Berezina.
Abyssosaurus represents the first reliable record of an aristonectid plesiosaur in Russia.
Berezin suggested the front flippers were used for steering and stabilization while the hind flippers were used for propulsion.
The broad thorax indicates a large lung volume, suggesting it could hold its breath for extended periods.
Berezin initially suggested Abyssosaurus was an aberrant member of the subfamily Aristonectinae within Cryptocleidoidea.
Later studies concluded that A. nataliae was a colymbosaurine, sister to Colymbosaurus, rather than an aristonectine.
Abyssosaurus is classified within the family Aristonectidae.
The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Abyssosaurus as Cryptoclididae.
Abyssosaurus was an extinct plesiosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous in what is now Russia.
Fossils of Abyssosaurus date to the Early Cretaceous period.
The strata containing the fossils are dated to the late or upper Hauterivian age of the Early Cretaceous.
The time range for Abyssosaurus is recorded as the Hauterivian, spanning from 132.6 to 125.77 million years ago.
It is debated whether Abyssosaurus was a basal aristonectid or related to Colymbosaurus, with later studies supporting the latter.
